# Corrie

*Apprentice Pilot*

## Personality

Careful, earnest and anxious to get everything right; she writes notes on the back of her hand.

## Lore

Corrie is nineteen and an apprentice pilot of the sea wardens, learning to take ships through the gap under Kor, the newest and boldest of the full wardens. She is careful, earnest and anxious to get everything right. She writes notes on the back of her hand in ink, tide times and warnings and things Kor has said, and by evening her left hand is usually blue to the wrist. Every night she copies the day's notes into a little oilcloth-covered book before she washes them off. She has filled four of these books. She has never lost one.

### The quay girl

Corrie grew up on the Inlet Quay with her mother, Rhona, who gutted fish for the smokehouses and raised her alone. Her father was a deckhand on a trading ship who sailed out before she was born and never came back to Goa Harbour; she has no wish to find him. Rhona died of a fever when Corrie was twelve, and after that the quay raised her. She ran errands for captains, carried messages to the Wardens' House, fetched rope and pies and lost cats, and learned the name of every boat and the temper of every skipper.

Four years ago, on a wet night, a stranger came down the gangplank of a coastal trader with one sea-chest and asked where she might find a bed. Corrie found her a loft above a net store, and that stranger was Esk, the sellsword. They have been friends ever since. Esk is the only person Corrie has ever met who is more careful than she is.

### Learning the gap

At seventeen Corrie talked her way onto the oars of the wardens' pilot boats, and she rowed for two years before anyone let her take a tiller. Last spring Kor became a full warden, and she was made his apprentice. Kor is cheerful and a little reckless; he whistles while he pilots and swears the tide likes him. Corrie learns more from his mistakes than from his advice, and keeps a separate page in her book for each kind. She admires him enormously and thinks he will drown one day if someone does not keep an eye on him, so she does.

### What she saw

Last month Corrie was in the pilot boat ahead of a timber ship, bringing it through the gap at slack water, when something large and dark passed beneath the ship. It was longer than the hull and moved against the tide, slowly, and then it was gone. Kor was looking the other way. When she told him, he laughed and said it was a cloud shadow. When she told the wardens, they were kind about it, which was worse. Only Halvard, the clerk, wrote it down, without a word, and Corrie does not know why.

Esk believed her at once, and then told her quietly that it was not the first: Esk has seen things of her own, far out beyond the gap, and describes them to no one but Corrie. Corrie writes those down too, on the back of her hand, and copies them into the back of her oilcloth book, on pages she has numbered and dated with great care. She thinks that if she can only make the record complete enough, the wardens will have to listen.

### What she wants and fears

Corrie wants to be a full sea warden, and to be the kind of warden people trust without question. She fears that she never will be now, that she will always be the apprentice who saw a monster in the gap. She fears much more that she was right, and that the next time it passes under a ship, the ship will not come out the other side.

### Hooks

A quest might keep watch with Corrie in the pilot boat at slack water to see the shadow again, help her lay her notes in front of the wardens, or bring Corrie and Halvard together to compare what each has written down.
